events.title: Romulus founds Rome, according to Roman tradition
events.description: Roman writers placed the city's foundation by Romulus on the Palatine on 21 April 753 BCE, a date fixed by the scholar Varro. Romans celebrated it each year as the Parilia.
events.html: Roman writers placed the city's foundation by Romulus on the Palatine on 21 April 753 BCE, a date fixed by the scholar Varro. Romans celebrated it each year as the Parilia.

events.title: Mark Antony fights Senate forces at the Battle of Mutina
events.description: At Mutina in Cisalpine Gaul, Senate forces under the consuls Pansa and Hirtius, with Octavian, fought Mark Antony, who was besieging Caesar's assassin Decimus Brutus there. Brutus was relieved, but later deserted by his troops and killed.

events.title: A debt pardon is recorded on the Laguna Copperplate Inscription
events.description: A copper plate dated to the Saka year 822 recorded the cancellation of a debt and named a leader of Tundun, usually identified with Tondo on Luzon. Found in 1989, it is the oldest known document from the Philippines.

events.title: Pope Urban II raises Pisa to an archdiocese
events.description: Pope Urban II elevated the Diocese of Pisa, founded in the 4th century, to the dignity of a metropolitan archdiocese, with its seat in the cathedral of the Assumption.
events.html: Pope Urban II elevated the Diocese of Pisa, founded in the 4th century, to the dignity of a metropolitan archdiocese, with its seat in the cathedral of the Assumption.

events.title: Three days of massacre in Lisbon come to an end
events.description: Rioting stirred up by Dominican friars killed between 1,000 and 4,000 New Christians, Jews forcibly converted in 1497. King Manuel I punished the city and had two of the friars executed.
events.html: Rioting stirred up by Dominican friars killed between 1,000 and 4,000 New Christians, Jews forcibly converted in 1497. King Manuel I punished the city and had two of the friars executed.

events.title: Babur defeats and kills Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat
events.description: Babur's 24,000 men, armed with muskets and artillery, defeated the 100,000-strong army of Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi, who died on the field with 20,000 of his men. The battle ended the Lodi dynasty and began Mughal rule in India.

events.title: The Wignacourt Aqueduct begins carrying water to Valletta
events.description: Built by the Order of Saint John to bring water from springs in Dingli and Rabat to the new capital Valletta, the aqueduct was inaugurated after work resumed in 1610. Named after Grand Master Alof de Wignacourt, it stayed in use until the 20th century.

events.title: Rama I founds Bangkok as Siam's new capital
events.description: The city pillar of Bangkok was erected on the east bank of the Chao Phraya, marking the official founding of the new royal capital. It replaced Thonburi across the river.
events.html: The city pillar of Bangkok was erected on the east bank of the Chao Phraya, marking the official founding of the new royal capital. It replaced Thonburi across the river.

events.title: Texans defeat Santa Anna at San Jacinto
events.description: Sam Houston's army surprised the Mexican camp and won in about eighteen minutes. Santa Anna was captured the next day and forced to order his troops out of Texas, securing its independence.

events.title: The Red Baron is shot down and killed near Amiens
events.description: Manfred von Richthofen, credited with 80 victories, was killed while pursuing an enemy aircraft over the Somme. Whether a Canadian pilot or Australian ground gunners fired the fatal shot is still debated.

events.title: Brasília is inaugurated as Brazil's capital
events.description: Built in under four years to plans by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer, Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital. It was meant to draw development into Brazil's interior.

song: the Portuguese; the republican movement; the Portuguese Republic
The national anthem of Portugal: a protest march of 1890 that became the anthem of the new Portuguese Republic in 1911.
